newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Auckland property confidence rises - survey.
newsitem.headline: NZ Auckland property confidence rises - survey.

text.p: Pessimism about the outlook for the Auckland commercial property market reduced markedly in most sectors and turned positive in the office sector during the August quarter, an Institute of Valuers survey showed on Tuesday.

The New Zealand Press Association reported that the biggest recovery came in the apartment sector, where only a net 10 percent of those surveyed expected a market deterioration in the November quarter.
This improved from the more than 50 percent who, in May, saw a deterioration in the August quarter.
The second largest reduction in pessimism occurred in industrial property, followed by retail.
In the office sector, net pessimism in May had turned to optimism by August.
The commercial property market, overall, was expected to remain steady by 58 percent of those surveyed, while 27 percent expected an improvement and 11 percent saw a deterioration.
The survey was the first conducted by the Massey University real estate analysis unit on behalf of the Institute of Valuers.
A panel of about 40 property professionals was asked how it saw the market performing in the next quarter in sale and rental price changes, volume of sales and leasings, and overall confidence.
The market, while expected to remain static ahead of the October 12 election as investors adopted a wait-and-see strategy, was tipped to improve after the election.

The greatest area of confidence was in office rentals, which were expected to go higher by a net 57 percent, while 19 percent expected industrial rentals to rise and four percent expected retail rentals to rise.
A net 20 percent expected office sale prices to rise, up from nil in May.
A net 19 percent expected retail values to fall, 15 percent expected a decline in apartment prices and four percent expected industrial prices to fall.
